about: Hand-written source for imagined.html (Who's Building It). Each theme: one early appearance in fiction from Not Boring's Sci-Fi Idea Bank (linked, never copied), a status with one dated primary source, one gap line, and the rules that pick companies from data.js. Rebuild with: python3 scripts/build_imagined.py. Method: data/imagined/README-METHOD.md.

themes.title: Space stations
themes.imagined: A brick satellite is launched by accident with people aboard, and they make a life in orbit.

evidence.fact: NASA marked 25 years of people living aboard the International Space Station without a break since 2 November 2000. At least 290 people from 26 countries have visited.

themes.gap: Every crewed station so far has been run by governments. No private station has launched yet, and Vast now aims for 2027.

themes.title: Mining in space
themes.imagined: Prospectors fly out to small asteroids and dig out their ore.

evidence.fact: NASA's OSIRIS-REx dropped a capsule in Utah holding 121.6 grams of rock and dust collected from the asteroid Bennu.

themes.gap: Only grams have come back, for science. No one has mined the Moon or an asteroid for material to use or sell.

themes.title: Moon bases
themes.imagined: People live and work at a permanent base on the Moon.

evidence.fact: NASA set out plans for a Moon Base near the lunar south pole. The robot landers meant to supply it, including Blue Moon MK1 and IM-3, were still in testing.

themes.gap: No one has landed on the Moon since 1972, and nothing permanent has been built there.

themes.title: Factories in orbit
themes.imagined: Factories circle the Earth, making things that are hard to make on the ground.

evidence.fact: Varda's W-1 capsule landed in Utah carrying crystals of the HIV drug ritonavir that were grown in orbit.

themes.gap: Only small test batches have come back. No factory makes goods in orbit for sale yet.

match.pattern: in-space manufactur|in-orbit manufactur|space-based manufactur|orbital manufactur|microgravity|space factory|re-?entry capsule|returnable capsule

themes.title: Power beamed from space
themes.imagined: A space station gathers sunlight and beams the energy down to the planets.

evidence.fact: Caltech's MAPLE test satellite beamed power wirelessly in orbit and sent a detectable amount to a receiver on a campus rooftop.

themes.gap: The power that reached the ground was barely detectable. No satellite sends useful electricity to Earth yet.

match.pattern: space-based solar|space solar power|power beaming|beam(ed|ing)? (power|energy)|wireless power transmission|reflected sunlight

themes.title: Watching Earth from orbit
themes.imagined: Pictures taken from orbit guide a military operation on the ground.

evidence.fact: The CORONA spy satellite program first brought film back from space in August 1960. That one mission photographed more of the Soviet Union than all earlier U-2 flights.

themes.gap: Live, sharp video of any spot on Earth on demand does not exist yet. Most pictures are snapshots taken as a satellite passes.

themes.title: Satellites that connect everyone
themes.imagined: A satellite that seems to hover over one spot relays signals around the world.

evidence.fact: NASA's Syncom 3, launched on 19 August 1964, was the first satellite parked over one spot on Earth. It relayed live television of the Tokyo Olympics.

themes.gap: Ordinary phones can now text and use a few apps through satellites, at low speeds. Normal calls and broadband from space are not here yet.

themes.title: Cheap rides to orbit
themes.imagined: Flying to low orbit becomes cheap and routine.

evidence.fact: On Starship's 15th flight the upper stage reached orbit, released 26 Starlink satellites and flew back to Starbase, where the launch tower caught it for the first time.

themes.gap: Falcon boosters now fly again and again, but no rocket is fully reusable yet: Flight 15's booster was lost and no caught ship has flown twice.

themes.title: Fusion power
themes.imagined: Power plants make energy by fusing atoms together.

evidence.fact: Livermore's National Ignition Facility got a record 8.6 megajoules of fusion energy from 2.08 megajoules of laser light on target, a gain of about four.

themes.gap: That gain counts only the laser light on target. The facility draws far more power, and no fusion machine has made electricity.

themes.title: Small nuclear reactors
themes.imagined: A tiny generator runs on atomic power.

evidence.fact: USS Nautilus cast off on 17 January 1955 and got underway on nuclear power, the Navy's history of the submarine records.

themes.gap: On land, the first new microreactors only reached zero-power tests in 2026. None sells electricity yet.

themes.title: Making rain
themes.imagined: A machine makes it rain when and where people want.

evidence.fact: Researchers measured the snowfall that cloud seeding produced over Idaho's mountains and reported the results in PNAS.

themes.gap: Seeding only works on clouds that already hold water. The WMO finds solid evidence mainly for winter clouds over mountains.

themes.title: Household robots
themes.imagined: An electric robot housemaid does the chores.

evidence.fact: 1X opened orders for NEO, a $20,000 home humanoid due to ship in 2026. For chores it has not learned, owners can book a 1X expert to guide it.

themes.gap: Robot vacuums and mowers each do one job. No robot yet does a home's chores on its own.

match.pattern: household robot|home robot|household chores|domestic chores|home humanoid|robots? for (the )?home

themes.title: Robot workers
themes.imagined: Factories turn out artificial workers, called robots, to do jobs for people.

evidence.fact: GXO signed a multi-year deal to use Agility's Digit humanoids, billed as the first formal commercial deployment of humanoid robots.

themes.gap: Humanoids do narrow, repetitive jobs at a few sites, and many deals are still pilots. Most robot workers are fixed arms.

themes.title: Factories that run themselves
themes.imagined: A factory works entirely on its own, with no one guiding it.

evidence.fact: FANUC says robot cells in its own factories machine parts without people for long hours, including nights and weekends.

themes.gap: People still supply materials, fix faults and run other shifts. No factory runs for good with nobody on site.

themes.title: 3D printing
themes.imagined: A machine prints the parts for a spaceship.

evidence.fact: Chuck Hull's patent for stereolithography, a machine that builds solid objects layer by layer, was issued on 11 March 1986.

themes.gap: Printers still can't turn out a finished product like a phone in one go. Most printed parts need finishing and assembly.

themes.title: Robot farmers
themes.imagined: Automatic electric machines take over the work of the farm.

fiction.work: Looking Forward: A Dream of the United States of the Americas in 1999
fiction.author: Arthur Bird

evidence.fact: Carbon Robotics says more than 200 growers in 15 countries use its machines, including the LaserWeeder, which kills weeds with lasers.

themes.gap: Robots do single jobs like weeding or milking. No robot yet farms on its own from planting to harvest.

match.pattern: agricultur\w* robot|farm robot|weeding robot|harvest(ing)? robot|autonomous tractor|robotic (harvest|weeding|farm)

themes.title: Self-driving vehicles
themes.imagined: Cars without steering wheels drive themselves.

evidence.fact: Waymo said it was giving more than 400,000 driverless rides a week across six US metro areas, with more than 20 million rides so far.

themes.gap: Most robotaxis still have steering wheels and drive only in mapped city zones. Nobody can buy a car that drives itself everywhere.

themes.title: Air taxis
themes.imagined: Electric flying taxis carry people across the city.

evidence.fact: Joby said it had finished a wide range of tests that count toward FAA certification, in the fifth and final stage of certifying its electric air taxi.

themes.gap: No air taxi has FAA certification yet, and regular paid service has not started at scale anywhere.

themes.title: Drone delivery
themes.imagined: Pilotless planes carry the mail.

evidence.fact: Zipline said it had passed two million commercial deliveries, with more than 125 million autonomous miles flown.

themes.gap: Drones carry small parcels over short hops in approved areas. Heavy, long-distance freight flights without pilots are not routine.

themes.title: Heat rays
themes.imagined: Invaders fire a beam of heat that burns whatever it touches.

evidence.fact: Israel's Defense Ministry and Rafael handed the first operational Iron Beam high-power laser system to the Israeli military.

themes.gap: Lasers work at short range against small threats and lose power in cloud or haze. Nothing like Wells's all-burning ray exists.

themes.title: Robot ships
themes.imagined: Ships cross the sea with no crew steering them.

evidence.fact: Saildrone sent a 20-meter uncrewed Surveyor to map about 13,000 square nautical miles of seafloor around the Mariana Islands for NOAA.

themes.gap: Robot boats map, patrol and even fight, but big ships still sail with crews, and most robot boats are watched by remote operators.

themes.title: Mind-controlled machines
themes.imagined: A brain implant lets a person see and control machines.

evidence.fact: China's drug regulator approved NEO, an implanted brain-computer interface that helps paralyzed patients grip with a pneumatic glove. Fudan calls it the world's first approved BCI for hand movement.

themes.gap: It restores one kind of grip, through a glove, for one injury. Moving a cursor or a robot arm by thought is still in trials.

themes.title: Gene editing
themes.imagined: Scientists reshape living things by working directly on their genes.

evidence.fact: The FDA approved Casgevy for sickle cell disease, the first approved medicine made with CRISPR gene editing.

themes.gap: Approved edits treat a few blood disorders in a patient's own cells. Editing embryos is barred in most countries.

match.pattern: gene editing|crispr|base editing|prime editing|gene writing|genome editing

themes.title: Robot surgeons
themes.imagined: A robot performs an operation on its own.

evidence.fact: A Johns Hopkins robot did a 17-task phase of gallbladder removal on a lifelike patient model without human help, after learning from surgery videos.

themes.gap: Surgeons still drive every robot used on patients. No robot has done a full operation on a living person by itself.

themes.title: Spare organs
themes.imagined: Human organs for transplant are grown outside the body.

evidence.fact: A patient lived 271 days without dialysis on a gene-edited pig kidney, the longest yet, before moving on to a human kidney.

themes.gap: No grown or pig organ is approved for routine use. The FDA has approved only simpler made tissue, such as a lab-grown blood vessel.

themes.title: Stopping aging
themes.imagined: A cheap drug sold at the corner store stops people from growing old.

evidence.fact: The FDA accepted the safety section of Loyal's application for LOY-002, a daily pill meant to extend the healthy lives of senior dogs.

themes.gap: No drug has been shown to slow or reverse aging in people. The nearest is a dog drug still waiting for FDA approval.

themes.title: Bringing back extinct animals
themes.imagined: A mammoth is brought back to life from the genes of the original.

evidence.fact: Colossal says its three wolf pups, the first born on 1 October 2024, are dire wolves brought back from extinction.

themes.gap: The pups are gray wolves with gene edits for dire-wolf traits. No mammoth-like calf has been born yet.
